title: LongCat 2.0: A 1.6T-Parameter Open Model Under MIT License
hook: 1.6 trillion total parameters, ~48B active, and released under the MIT license — one of the most permissively licensed large open-weight MoE models yet.
key_points: LongCat 2.0: 1.6T total parameters, roughly 48B active per token — a large sparse mixture-of-experts model.
Weights released under the MIT license, more permissive than the community or restricted licenses many large open models ship under.
Announced via a technical blog post and amplified across the open-model community (ModelScope, independent researchers).
content_html: Open-weight models at the trillion-parameter scale are no longer rare, but licensing terms still vary widely. LongCat 2.0 lands with both a large sparse mixture-of-experts design and one of the most permissive licenses going.
extra_html: LongCat 2.0 ships with 1.6 trillion total parameters and roughly 48 billion active per token, and — notably — the weights are released under the MIT license, more permissive than the community or restricted licenses many similarly large open models carry. The release was announced via a technical blog post and quickly amplified across the open-model community, including ModelScope. For teams choosing an open MoE model to build on, the license terms are often as consequential as the benchmark numbers. Reported on r/LocalLLaMA, 2026-07-05.

related.title: What Is a Mixture of Experts?
related.hook: Instead of running every input through one big network, route each token to a few specialist sub-networks - total capacity grows without proportional compute.

related.title: Mixtral of Experts
related.hook: Mixtral packs 8 experts per layer but routes each token through only 2, so you get the capacity of a ~47B model at the compute cost of a ~13B one - open weights included.

related.title: DeepSeek-V4: Sparse Attention, Million-Token Default
related.hook: DeepSeek-V4 makes a 1M-token context window the default and pairs token-wise compression with sparse attention, so long-context inference no longer pays the usual compute and memory tax.

flashcards.back_html: 1.6 trillion total parameters with roughly 48B active per token (a large sparse mixture-of-experts model), released under the permissive MIT license.

flashcards.prompt: Why does the MIT license matter for a model of LongCat 2.0's scale?

choices.text: It's notably more permissive than the community or restricted licenses many large open-weight models ship under, easing commercial and downstream use
MIT licensing is required for any model over 1 trillion parameters
It means the model's weights are encrypted
It has no practical effect compared to other open licenses

flashcards.explanation_html: Many large open-weight releases use community or restricted licenses with usage caveats. MIT is one of the most permissive options, which matters for anyone wanting to build on or commercialize the model.
